A lot of what you might come up with would apply equal well to women; such things would comprise what makes an adult. It's much harder to come up with answers that apply mostly, or exclusively, to men.

One such answer is suggested by biology; a distinct population of fifty women and two men may survive, while a population of fifty men and two women is doomed. When push comes to shove, and an existential threat emerges which can wipe out a tribe and all that it knows and stands for, is the moment when the men become expendable in the face of whatever must be done. Cultures which have bred men who will respond this way have endured far better than those which haven't, and we, as the progeny of many millennium's survivors, have inherited this attribute.

The "women and children first" stuff is not a myth. Men are men, in part, because they have what's necessary, perhaps near the surface, or perhaps buried deep somewhere inside themselves. Those truly without it are, I think, legitimately less qualified for the role.

This is just one example of course, a small but important part of a much bigger picture. I wish I had more to offer beyond that.
